I reckon it's mid-June now, and I've got my 1.7 mu plot ready for maize. Fifty years I've been doing this — since I was 15 — so I know this land pretty well. It's not much, 1.7 mu, but it's what I have, and at my age I'm not looking to take big risks.

My son works off-farm in the county town, so it's mostly just me and my wife at home. That means family labor is tight, especially if she needs to help her sister's family with their harvest too. I can't afford to hire much help — not on 1.7 mu — so whatever I do, I have to manage mostly with my own two hands.

**What I'm planting:** Maize, same as always. I'll plant around June 18th, right after the wheat harvest finishes in the village. I don't grow wheat myself — my plot's too small and my back's not what it used to be — so I just wait until the neighbors' wheat comes off and the custom tillage guy has time to come by. I'll hire him for rotary tillage, maybe 60 yuan for the plot. For seed, I'll buy hybrid maize from the village supply shop. Last year I used a variety called Zhengdan 958, got about 420 jin per mu. Cost me about 40 yuan per mu for the seed. I'll stick with that — why change what works? The extension fellow mentioned some new variety, but the seed costs more and I'm not experimenting at my age.

**Fertilizer:** Last year I put down about 15 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and topdressed 8 kg of urea at the jointing stage. The crop looked fine. This year, fertilizer prices are up a bit, so I'm thinking of cutting back slightly — maybe 12-13 kg of compound fertilizer as base, and I'll skip the topdress unless the leaves look really yellow. The extension guy says I should do 15 kg plus topdress for 500 kg/mu yield, but honestly, I can't afford to chase that. I'd rather get a steady 400 kg/mu than spend extra money I might not get back. I'll use some phosphorus too — maybe 5 kg P per mu mixed in with the base fertilizer. No potassium — my soil's got enough, never seen deficiency symptoms.

**Irrigation:** I've got well water, but pumping costs money — about 15 yuan per mu each time. The weather's been okay so far, some rain in May. For maize, I'll probably irrigate once at the big trumpet stage if July turns dry. If it rains enough, I might not irrigate at all. Cash is tight, so every pumping has to be justified.

**Pesticide:** I'll spray herbicide once before emergence — acetochlor or something similar, costs about 20 yuan per mu. For insects, I won't spray unless I see armyworms or aphids. At my age I walk the field every morning anyway, so I'll keep an eye out. If I see damage, I'll buy one spray, maybe 15 yuan. No preventive spraying — that's money down the drain.

**Labor:** Planting will take me about 3 days if I do it by hand (broadcasting and covering), or I could hire the planter with the tillage guy for an extra 20 yuan. I'll probably plant by hand to save money — I've got time. Fertilizer application, 1 day. Weeding if needed, 2 days. Harvesting, another 2-3 days. Maybe 10 family days total. No hired labor except the tillage guy.

**Yield expectation:** If the weather cooperates and I get that one irrigation in, I expect about 400 kg per mu. That's conservative, but at 65 I don't count on good years. A normal year gives me about 680 kg total from my 1.7 mu, which at 2.2 yuan/kg brings in about 1,500 yuan. After inputs, maybe 900-1,000 yuan clear. It's not much, but combined with my son's off-farm income, we get by.
